mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS average > 2% over the past quarter
failure_condition: In rising-rate regimes, 20-day forward returns are non-negative with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS outpacing CPIAUCSL inflation) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger wage growth supports consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > CPIAUCSL inflation rate over the prior month
failure_condition: Pay growth acceleration is not statistically significant (p > 0.1) or 60-day returns are negative in 70% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below the prior 4 quarters signals a demand contraction, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant negative returns in 5-day windows following INDPRO declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in RSAFS above 300 million dollars indicates reduced inventory pressure and supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: RSAFS increases are not associated with higher 20-day forward returns (correlation < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return turns negative due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: No negative 60-day returns observed after the crossing in non-recessionary regimes (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6% predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces participation and dampens risk aversion.
Consecutive months of rising HOUST (retail sales) above 500K units imply strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: No significant positive returns in 20-day windows following such demand acceleration (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the aggregate macro momentum (GDPC1 growth rate minus CPIAUCSL inflation rate) turns positive for the first time in 30 days, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > CPIAUCSL monthly inflation over the past 30 days
failure_condition: The 20-day return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
